fieldValues.title: Polarity is assigned per domain and per axis: an axis-in-domain record
fieldValues.decision_question: Where does a tension's yin and yang live, given that the same pole may be yang in one boundary and yin in a narrower one?
fieldValues.context: Problem: polarity is global today. A pole is yang wherever the Initiator archetype leans toward it or wherever it refines such a pole (ruling 2026-10-20, srs-context cc05d4c9). That cannot say 'Portability is yang in Semantic records but yin in a narrower boundary'. A domain's axes are also 'the first three tensions in its container outline', which is arrangement standing in for meaning, against the principle 'Affirmed meaning over fixed arrangement'. Answers: SP-98 (poles put up for affirmation one at a time, with no orthogonality test). Raised in the owner's walk of the Domains view (clerk#129, srs-lab#16), 2026-10-22.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: 1. An axis-in-domain record per domain (chosen). 2. A yang-in relation only, from pole to domain, one per tension per context: lighter, but a relation has no Suggested/Affirmed layers. 3. Keep global polarity and mark tensions without it as unrecorded: zooming in cannot flip a pole.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Owner, 2026-10-22: 'Ideally, we need to assign a yin/yang pole. These will again be relative to the axis and domain. The same pole may be yang when we zoom in to a different boundary.' Chosen: an axis record per domain. New method type com.semanticops.method/axis-in-domain v1. Fields: title, line (1-3, line 1 at the bottom), summary. Relations: refines to its tension, in-domain to the domain record, and a new yang-pole to one of that tension's two poles, exactly one of each. A domain has at most three affirmed axes, on distinct lines, with distinct tensions. A domain with no affirmed axes inherits its parent's. A narrower domain flips a pole by holding its own axis for the same tension with the other yang-pole. Polarity exists only on an axis. The global Initiator/refines rule only suggests yang-pole on agent-suggested axes. 'First three tensions in the outline' is retired as the rule for axes. This supersedes the global-polarity part of the 2026-10-20 ruling; the line pairing it fixed stays.
fieldValues.rationale: Polarity is a judgement made in relation, within one domain and on one axis, so it needs a record that can be suggested, affirmed, commented on and set aside like every other method judgement. A record also moves the axes from arrangement (outline order) to meaning. The change goes in through package relations, with no core change (standing rule D3-rule).
fieldValues.revisit_when: When a domain needs more than three axes, or when the untraced boundaries are given domain records and their axes must be placed.
fieldValues.next_steps: 1. Ratify this in a session. 2. clerk: method package 1.1.0 (type, line field, yang-pole relation), check-method rules, the domain field and the set-axis / unset-axis acts. 3. srs-programme: install the package from its bundle; agent-suggested axes for Stance and Semantic records. 4. srs-lab: the Domains view and the Tensions view read axes and yang from the clerk. 5. srs-context: update concept cc05d4c9.
